subject: Multi-cloud entry packs & region prioritization — decision request
messages:
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: awong@amazon.com, priya.shah@microsoft.com, gcp-partners@google.com
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: Multi-cloud entry packs & region prioritization — decision request

Team + partners,

Following up from last week's sync: we need to lock the initial marketplace SKUs and the first tranche of regions for each cloud so listings, pricing, and co-sell enablement workstreams can proceed. Draft attached (redwood_marketplace_entrypack_draft_v2.xlsx) — high level summary below.

Ask: please review and confirm decisions by EOD Thursday so legal/pricing can start the packaging docs. If partners have constraints, flag them inline.

Summary (draft):
- Entry packs (per-cloud):
  * AWS: metered SaaS (1 SKU - Standard), 1 subscription-level SKU (Reserved-1y)
  * Azure: ARM SaaS offer + Azure IP co-sell tagging (1 SKU Standard, 1 SKU Enterprise)
  * GCP: Marketplace container image SaaS (1 SKU Standard) + Marketplace SaaS metering for enterprise trials
- Regional priority (phase 1): US-East, US-West, EU-West1 (for GCP), UK-South (Azure)
- Packaging: single feature-tier approach w/ add-on modules (embedding-store, private-key-integration) rather than many skinny SKUs
- Commercial: list pricing parity target across clouds, with marketplace fees baked into MSDP where possible

Open decision areas I want us to confirm:
1) SKU granularity — keep to 1-2 SKUs per cloud or add a lightweight "Developer" SKU?
2) Regions for phase 1 — do we align strictly by cloud-recommended regions or prioritize customer demand (CloudMarket ask: US, Canada, Germany)?
3) Co-sell readiness — Amazon asked for additional telemetry hooks; do we include now or stage?

Attaching: entry pack draft + co-sell checklist.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Partnerships (Marketplaces)
Redwood Inference

+1 415-555-0192

Laura / team,

Quick read-through — strong preference for keeping SKU count minimal for launch. Operationally we'll pay for extra complexity (metering instrumentation, entitlement checks) across three clouds. My suggestions inline in the attached sheet, but high-level:
- Keep 1 primary SKU per cloud (Standard) + one Enterprise SKU for commitment pricing. Skip Developer SKU for now; use trial vouchers instead.
- Regions: prioritize based on existing customer requests + co-sell potential. For CloudMarket specifically, add Canada (ca-central-1) to phase 1 for AWS and ask Azure to enable Canada Central.
- Telemetry hooks: we should include a thin telemetry contract now (request IDs, usage events) — not full trace export. That keeps co-sell enablement moving without heavy infra work.

I'll take owner on the SKU instrumentation checklist.

— Karthik
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Adding notes from GTM lens — we need to be explicit about which packaging entitles customers to co-sell motions (AWS: ISV Accelerate, Azure: IP co-sell eligible SKU, GCP: Verified Partner listing). Also some practical items:
- Marketplace listing names must match our public product page; suggest canonical naming: "Redwood Inference — Standard" and "Redwood Inference — Enterprise" to avoid mapping confusion.
- Trials: Azure requires a 30-day trial artifact to enable IP co-sell sign-off; GCP wants a billing-enabled trial for metered SaaS. We'll need legal templates adjusted.
- For EU and UK we should confirm data locality options (single-tenant instances vs. regional tenancy).

I can coordinate legal language with pricing if you give me sign-off on the 1–2 SKU approach.

Laura / team,

Thanks for the draft — happy to support. A couple notes from AWS Partner/Co-sell perspective:
- AWS prefers metered SaaS listings with a single Standard SKU for ease of procurement; offering a 1y reserved SKU is fine as a single subscription option.
- Region ask: US & EU priority is sensible; Canada addition is allowed but requires marketplace registration for CA region which adds ~3 business days to validation.
- Telemetry: we need a lightweight usage event and entitlement confirmation endpoint (we give the exact spec in the partner portal). We can sign an NDA addendum for the telemetry contract if that helps accelerate.

I'll provide the exact telemetry spec and marketplace listing checklist by COB today.

Thanks everyone — summary / decisions locked for phase 1 below (action owners included).

Decisions:
- SKU approach: 1 Standard SKU + 1 Enterprise (commit) SKU per cloud. No Developer SKU for launch; we'll enable trials via marketplace trial artifacts and promo codes. (Owner: Marissa)
- Telemetry: implement a thin usage/entitlement webhook now (spec from AWS). Instrumentation owner: Karthik (deliverable: telemetry endpoints + sample payloads by 2026-09-10).
- Regions (phase 1): US-East (AWS), US-West (GCP), EU-West1 (GCP), UK-South (Azure), Canada (AWS) — we added Canada per CloudMarket ask; procurement to validate timelines. (Owner: Laura for procurement coordination)
- Packaging & naming: canonical names: "Redwood Inference — Standard" and "Redwood Inference — Enterprise". GTM assets to reflect exact marketplace names. (Owner: Marissa)
- Legal / pricing: Marissa to shepherd pricing language into marketplace contracts and coordinate with legal for marketplace-specific trial artifacts. (Owner: Marissa + Legal)

Next steps / deadlines:
- Karthik to post telemetry spec + checklist by 2026-09-03.
- Marissa to finalize marketplace listing names and trial artifacts by 2026-09-07.
- Laura to open CloudMarket procurement ticket and confirm Canada validation timeline by 2026-09-02.

If there are objections, flag them in-thread by EOD Monday. Otherwise we'll move to PRD and legal intake next week.

Laura Bennett
Head of Partnerships (Marketplaces)
Redwood Inference
